name: Kunsthalle Wien
funding: City of Vienna (MA 7) core funding. Sponsors: Dorotheum, Ottakringer, Vöslauer, Winzerhof Dockner, Das Teppich Werk, Ton & Bild. 2026 programme support from Institut français and the Mondriaan Fund.
records_note: Shows funders and sponsors as logos under 2026 headings; it posts no annual report, accounts or board list.

name: Leopold Museum
funding: Federal ministry subsidy. Sponsors: Siwacht, Post, PORR, Arbeiterkammer Wien, Dorotheum, im Kinsky; partner Wiener Städtische (insurer).
watch: Independent private foundation created with state funding in 1994 to house Rudolf Leopold's Schiele collection. Subject to Austrian Federal Art Restitution Act scrutiny regarding provenance of early 20th-century Austrian modernist works.
records_note: Names two partners in text and shows the rest as logos; it posts no annual report, accounts or foundation board.

name: mumok
funding: Federal museum funded by the Republic of Austria. Sponsors: Dorotheum, UNIQA, Gerngross, legero united. Patrons: Ludwig foundations and the Art Mentor Foundation Lucerne.
watch: Austrian federal museum situated in the MuseumsQuartier. Financial statements audited by the Austrian Court of Audit (Rechnungshof); corporate partners (Audi, Erste Bank) adhere to federal cultural patronage compliance codes.
records_note: Posts yearly culture reports and audited accounts for 2019 to 2023 and names its nine trustees; sponsors appear as undated logos.

name: The Hepworth Wakefield
funding: £4.2M income in 2024-25; Arts Council England and Wakefield Council are partners. Bloomberg Philanthropies, trusts and Grand Central Rail also give.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Supporters page names partners and funders undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Yorkshire Sculpture Park
funding: Core funding from Arts Council England, Wakefield Council, Roger Evans, the Liz and Terry Bramall Foundation and Dunard Fund. Corporate partners: HSBC, Sandal MINI and BMW, Luscombe Drinks, Archivist.
watch: The ASA banned two HSBC climate adverts in October 2022; HSBC is a current corporate partner. No protest at YSP turned up.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Our supporters page names funders and partners undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Te Papa
funding: NZ$85M revenue (2024-25), Crown 52%. Its current partners page lists Panasonic, Bloomberg, Samsung, MyLotto and gaming-machine trusts PubCharity and Lion Foundation.
watch: Both raise money from gaming machines. Named Te Taiao | Nature grant partners at its 2019 opening and again in the 2024-25 annual report.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2000-01 to 2024-25 with Auditor-General accounts, names its eight board members and lists partners without a date.

name: Audain Art Museum
funding: Audain Foundation and Polygon Homes. Endowment founders include Onni Group, Whistler Blackcomb Foundation and the Resort Municipality of Whistler. The April 2026 gala raised C$1.5M.
watch: Purpose-built museum in Whistler, BC housing British Columbia art.
records_note: Posts four annual reports (2020-21 to 2023-24) on Issuu, lists 18 trustees, and names endowment founders by giving tier; no financial statements found.

name: Plug In ICA
funding: Canada Council, Manitoba Arts Council, Winnipeg Arts Council and the federal government. Corporate supporters: RBC Foundation and Johnston Group, a benefits firm.
watch: First non-profit Institute of Contemporary Art in Canada.
records_note: Lists its board and names members and supporters on a 2025-26 recognition page; sponsor logos are undated, and no annual reports or accounts are posted.

name: TarraWarra Museum of Art
funding: Founded by Marc and Eva Besen (retail), whose family foundation endows it. Sponsors: Arnold Bloch Leibler, Chubb, Aon, Four Pillars Gin. Victoria and Yarra Ranges Council fund education.
watch: First major privately endowed public museum in Australia (Yarra Valley).
records_note: Names its eight-member board and shows sponsors as undated logos; its policies page posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: Kunsthalle Zürich
funding: Funded by members and patrons, City of Zürich and Canton Zürich subsidies, the Ernst Göhner, Foksal Gallery, Gubler Hablützel and Luma foundations, and Ringier AG.
watch: Swiss Re and Bloomberg, named in the old note, are not on the 2025 supporter list. No controversy found among the funders listed.
records_note: Annual reports 2015 to 2025 include audited accounts; a dated 2025 supporter list and the full board are on the about page.

name: Migros Museum
funding: Institution of the Migros-Kulturprozent, carried by the Migros cooperative federation, which pays a turnover-based sum into culture since 1957. The sheet lists CHF 12 tickets and no public funder.
watch: Unique Swiss model established by Migros cooperative founder Gottlieb Duttweiler, mandating 1% of cooperative wholesale turnover to culture and education.
why_flagged: Migros owns fuel supplier Migrol: CHF 1.3bn of CHF 31.9bn group sales in 2025, about 4%. Fuel is not its main line.
records_note: The museum publishes nothing itself; parent Migros-Genossenschafts-Bund publishes reports 2020 to 2025, audited accounts and its board. No donor list.

name: MoMA (The Museum of Modern Art)
funding: Admissions, individual board donations, Bloomberg Philanthropies, Hyundai Card, UNIQLO (UNIQLO NYC Nights), Cartier, Bank of America, Chanel, Volkswagen Group, Allianz.
watch: Leon Black still a trustee after Epstein payments; Fink, Crown and Dubin named in Strike MoMA and the 2024 sit-in.
why_flagged: Leon Black still a trustee after Epstein payments; Fink, Crown and Dubin named in Strike MoMA and the 2024 sit-in.
records_note: Its Year in Review reports run from 2014 to 2025, with audited statements and Form 990 posted; the donor list seen is dated 2016.
other_findings: Epstein link · Leon Black · documented: Leon Black is a MoMA trustee and was its board chair until 2021. DOJ files show Epstein guided his $115 million purchase of Picasso's Buste de Femme (Marie-Thérèse) from Gagosian, a sculpture shown in MoMA's 2015 "Picasso Sculpture" show. Black paid Epstein $158 million from 2012 to 2017, according to a 2021 Dechert review for Apollo, or $170 million for tax and estate planning by Senator Ron Wyden's count, and he denies the sexual abuse allegations against him. Black stepped down as chair in 2021 and is still a MoMA trustee in 2026. In 2023 he paid the US Virgin Islands $62.5 million to settle Epstein-related claims; the settlement notes he was not accused of wrongdoing. | Epstein link · Glenn Dubin · documented: Glenn Dubin is a MoMA trustee, and the New York Post reported in October 2019 that MoMA had named a fourth-floor gallery after him and his wife, Eva Andersson-Dubin. In September 2020 the US Virgin Islands attorney general gave notice that she would subpoena him, and he was named in documents unsealed in January 2024. Eva Andersson-Dubin is Epstein's ex-girlfriend, and Virginia Giuffre alleged that Epstein trafficked her to Dubin in 2001, when she was 16, which the Dubins categorically deny. In November 2019 the Guerrilla Girls called for Dubin and Leon Black to be removed from the board and for their galleries to be draped in black. MoMA did not comment. | Epstein link · Ronald Lauder · documented: Ronald Lauder is a former MoMA board chair and is still a trustee. He is mentioned more than 900 times in the DOJ files released in January 2026, including a 2014 email that sent Epstein the possession and loan agreement for a Kurt Schwitters work Lauder co-owns with Leon Black. In 2017 Lauder's and Epstein's assistants arranged meetings and calls, and Epstein's assistant said Epstein wanted to see two years of Lauder's tax returns and his will; ARTnews found no direct communication between the two men. Lauder has not commented publicly, and his representative did not respond to ARTnews.
